g.text: Urban green spaces and student well-being
Access to green space is often associated with better mental
health. For university students, small moments outdoors may
offer a meaningful break from demanding academic routines.
This study explores how the frequency and quality of visits
to campus green spaces relate to self-reported well-being.
1. How often do students use campus green spaces?
2. What activities do they engage in during these visits?
3. How do visits relate to perceived stress levels?
A mixed-method approach will combine an anonymous survey
with short interviews. Participants will be recruited across
year levels to capture a range of campus experiences.
Survey responses will be analyzed descriptively. Interview
transcripts will be coded for recurring themes and patterns.
